full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the appellant as plaintiff instituted Title suit No.38 of 1999 before the Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for declaration that the plaintiff is a lawful owner of the plot measuring 325 sq. yards being plot No.21/1, Avenue No.3, Haji Road, Block-G, section 2, Mirpur Housing State, PS Mirpur, District-Dhaka and defendant No.3 has no right and title and interest to allot the said plot in favour of defendant No.1 who has not acquired any right, title, interest by virtue of revised allotment order being letter No.155/ 80/50/2(3)SC dated 4-1-1999. The plaintiff stated, inter alia, that he is a local permanent resident of Mirpur and his ancestral property was acquired by the then Government of East Pakistan for development of Mirpur Housing Estate for the purpose of settlement of all persons who were coming from India for permanent residence in Pakistan (East Pakistan) and for that purpose the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Land Acquisition) acquired the land measuring 962 acres under mouja Senpara Parbata comparing CS Khatian No.199 SA khatian No.428 CS and SA dag No.419 belonging to the plaintiff and his family in LA Case No.13/1959-60. The plaintiff having been uprooted from his ancestral land, the Government allotted a plot of land vide allotment letter No.600 /CS dated 18-1-1987 measuring 325 sq. yds. being plot No.21/1, Block-G, Haji Road, section 2, Mirpur Housing Estate, Dhaka and paid the entire selami by challan and erected pucca construction and erected boundary wall also and took electric and gas connection and has been living with his family members since 1987. But defendant No.1 with main fide intention in collusion with the officials of Mirpur Housing Estate obtained a revised allotment letter for 193.33 sq. yds. in plot No.21/2 on 4-1-1999 by curtailing land of the plaintiff which was not acted upon at any point of time and no delivery of possession was ever made.
